summary: An offshore Lake Huron pier light built in 1877-78 to mark a reef at the mouth of Saginaw Bay, rebuilt in brick in 1899-1900 and now restored by a volunteer association.

access.note: Offshore pier reachable only by boat; owner's licensed tours on Saturdays in season.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree: Pepper dates the crib sinking to Sunday 12 Aug 1877 but says construction began July 1878 (internally inconsistent; PARLA timeline says July 1877); PARLA history page says Congress appropriated $82,151.14 in 1856, which looks wrong against Pepper's 1873/1876 and was left out. Lens removal 1941 (PARLA history) vs 1942 (Pepper, timeline). Pier concrete casing appears under both 1933 and 1937 in Pepper. Current optic given variously (acrylic 1985, LED 2011, 200 mm glass in USLHS). Light characteristic and range not verified from a current Light List. Charles Kimball of the 1925 Bulletin is linked to Charles A. Kimball by name and shared stations only; the Bulletin gives no middle initial. Lauchling/Towns names in the 1917 Bulletin are OCR-garbled and the Commissioner 1917 table lists them by initials; the Bulletin's Feb 21 date is read from an interleaved two-column OCR, matched by position. Fog-signal hours from the 1900 report cover fiscal year ended June 1900. No NRHP nomination text was available (not digitised). One Chronicling America hit (Alma Record, 1886-11-05) mentions an assistant keeper only; not used. Pepper (2002) says tours were not available; PARLA home page says 2026 season has ended. PARLA states a Fresnel was lit on 23 May 2026 for a broadcast; not independently verified. Access: climbable only on licensed tours.
